title: Affine completed kernel annihilation makes the completed coherent ideal product zero
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, and $a:F\to G$ a morphism of coherent modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $t\in\mathbb N$. For every affine open $U$, take the inverse limit $a_U$ of the section maps of the $I$-adic quotient system of $a$ (positive level $n+1$). Suppose $K(U)^t$ annihilates $\ker(a_U)$. Then $H=K^t\ker(a)$, with the image definition of ideal product [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], is coherent and $H/I^{n+1}H=0$ for every $n\geq0$. No completion equivalence or local faithfulness is assumed.

proof.text: Kernels of coherent maps are coherent. Ideal powers and their products are quasi-coherent; on the Noetherian affine basis the ideal product is finite. Thus H is coherent.

Affine sections identify the kernel and ideal product with the corresponding finite module kernel and ideal multiple. The natural identification of finite-module completion with tensoring by the flat completed ring preserves this kernel and the image defining the ideal product.

The natural affine-limit comparison identifies the completed section map with a_U. Its kernel is annihilated by K(U)^t, so the completed ideal product from the preceding step is zero. Every positive quotient is a quotient of that completion and hence has zero affine sections. The affine opens form a basis, so each quotient sheaf is zero.
